elements.quote: Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang for cohort studies, case-control studies, and cross-sectional studies up to March 16, 2023, to conduct a meta-analysis of global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the study is a meta-analysis and identifies it as a systematic review in the title and methods.

elements.quote: Background There is a significant increase in the number of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection reports in various countries. However, the trend of reinfection rate over time is not clear.
elements.reason: The abstract provides the background and objective regarding the trend of reinfection rate over time.

elements.quote: Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang for cohort studies, case-control studies, and cross-sectional studies up to March 16, 2023
elements.reason: The abstract specifies inclusion criteria regarding study types (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) but does not explicitly list exclusion criteria in the abstract text.

elements.quote: Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang... up to March 16, 2023
elements.reason: The abstract lists the information sources and the date the search was last conducted.

elements.quote: The risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the tools used to assess risk of bias.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, country, study type, and study population, and time-varying reinfection rates of SARS-CoV-2 were estimated using meta-regression.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the methods used to present and synthesize results (subgroup analyses, meta-regression).

elements.quote: Result A total of 55 studies involving 111,846 cases of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection were included.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies and participants.

elements.quote: The pooled SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate was 0.94% (95% CI : 0.65 -1.35%).
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcome (pooled reinfection rate) with confidence intervals.

elements.quote: The pooled SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate was 0.94% (95% CI : 0.65 -1.35%).
elements.reason: The abstract reports the summary estimate and its 95% confidence interval.

elements.quote: SARS-CoV-2 is at risk of reinfection and the Omicron variant has a higher reinfection rate than other currently known variants.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect and which group (Omicron) is favored in subgroup comparisons.
The abstract text does not contain a section or statement summarizing limitations of the included evidence.

elements.quote: The results of this study could help guide public health measures and vaccination strategies in response to the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number.

elements.quote: The WHO study published in Nature [1, 3] also suggested that accurately tracking SARS-CoV-2 and its impact had been challenging.
elements.reason: The Introduction describes general uncertainties in tracking SARS-CoV-2 but does not explicitly mention the specific uncertainty regarding reinfection rate trends found in the Abstract.

elements.quote: posing a serious threat to the health of populations in all countries... The fact that SARS-CoV-2 is still mutating indicates that it remains a global health threat.
elements.reason: The Introduction explains the general importance and threat of the pandemic, but the specific need for this reinfection review is not explicitly detailed in the Introduction section.
The Introduction section does not mention or compare with previous systematic reviews, although the Discussion notes advantages compared to previous meta-analyses.
This is an observational review of reinfection rates, not a review of intervention effects.
This is an observational review, not a complex intervention review requiring a logic model.

elements.quote: The inclusion criteria were: (1) Conformed to research questions, i.e., studies that estimated the reinfection rate of SARS-CoV-2 or we could calculate it based on the data provided in the paper; (2) The study design included cohort study, case-control study, and descriptive study; (3) The study fited our working definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection... reinfection working definition in this study was based on a positive laboratory result at least 90 days after laboratory confirmation of primary infection
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies study designs, question framework components, and follow-up requirements (90-day interval) within the inclusion criteria.

elements.quote: To avoid language bias, the search was not limited to any language... (4) Grey literature, including a range of documents not controlled by commercial publishing organizations.
elements.reason: Language and publication status (grey literature) are specified, but dissemination year is not mentioned in the eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: Therefore, we excluded the above literature with the number of unreported infections... Reports excluded: ... the number of first infections was not reported
elements.reason: The review excludes studies with unreported outcomes but does not distinguish this from studies where outcomes were not measured.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed by meta-regression to fit stratified rates of reinfection based on variables such as variant and country... we also used spline regression to fit time-varying reinfection rates
elements.reason: Synthesis groups (variant, country, time) are specified and align with the review objectives (regions, populations, time trends).

elements.quote: reinfection working definition in this study was based on a positive laboratory result at least 90 days... advised from WHO and US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
elements.reason: Rationale is provided for the reinfection definition restriction, but no rationale is provided for the sample size (<20) exclusion criterion.

elements.quote: We searched for papers published on PubMed, Web of Science, Medline(Ovid), Embase(Ovid), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure(CNKI), Wanfang using 'COVID-19' , '2019-nCoV' , 'SARS-COV-2' , 'Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2' , 'reinfection' , 'recurrence' , 'repeat positive' and 'repeat infections' as keywords, from January 1, 2020 to March 16, 2023 (Additional file 2).
elements.reason: The full search strategy is not reported in the text; it is referred to as 'Additional file 2', the content of which is not provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: To avoid language bias, the search was not limited to any language.
elements.reason: Language limit is described and justified ('To avoid language bias'), but the date limit justification is not explicitly linked to eligibility criteria in the text.

elements.quote: The search strategy we used was based on previous studies, and the process of literature screening and information extraction strictly followed PRISMA standards.
elements.reason: Reference to 'previous studies' is vague and does not cite specific published search approaches or filters used.

elements.quote: We searched for papers published on PubMed, Web of Science, Medline(Ovid), Embase(Ovid), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure(CNKI), Wanfang...
elements.reason: No natural-language processing or text-analysis tools are specified for identifying or refining search terms.

elements.quote: if the included article was neither in English nor in Chinese and did not provide an English abstract or full text, we used an online translator (Google Translate) for translation.
elements.reason: Google Translate was used for translating articles, not for translating search strings between sources.

elements.quote: We searched for papers published on PubMed, Web of Science, Medline(Ovid), Embase(Ovid), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure(CNKI), Wanfang...
elements.reason: No validation of the search strategy is described in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: We searched for papers published on PubMed, Web of Science, Medline(Ovid), Embase(Ovid), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure(CNKI), Wanfang...
elements.reason: No peer review of the search strategy is described in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: We searched for papers published on PubMed, Web of Science, Medline(Ovid), Embase(Ovid), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure(CNKI), Wanfang...
elements.reason: The final conceptual structure and explorations used to develop the search strategy are not described.

elements.quote: The reviewers independently (CY, Z-WH, H-XY, C-MS, LX, H-HP) screened the literature based on inclusion and exclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The text lists the reviewers who screened the literature but does not explicitly state the number of reviewers who screened each record (e.g., 'two reviewers').

elements.quote: The reviewers independently (CY, Z-WH, H-XY, C-MS, LX, H-HP) screened the literature based on inclusion and exclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that reviewers screened the literature independently.

elements.quote: Conflicts were resolved by other independent reviewers (ZT Y-CH).
elements.reason: The text describes the process for resolving conflicts during screening.

elements.quote: If the paper did not mention the reinfection variant, we classified the reinfection variants based on the WHO standards according to the study period.
elements.reason: The text describes classification based on standards, but does not mention contacting study investigators to obtain or confirm eligibility information.

elements.quote: if the included article was neither in English nor in Chinese and did not provide an English abstract or full text, we used an online translator (Google Translate) for translation.
elements.reason: The text reports the method used to translate articles for eligibility assessment.

elements.quote: used an online translator (Google Translate) for translation.
elements.reason: While a translation tool is mentioned, no automation tools for the screening process (e.g., screening software) are described.
No externally derived classifiers were used in the study selection process.
No internally derived classifiers were used in the study selection process.
No machine-learning prioritisation tools were used in the study selection process.
No crowdsourcing platforms were used in the study selection process.
No previously screened datasets were used to eliminate records.

The text specifies the number of reviewers for screening ('The reviewers independently (CY, Z-WH, H-XY, C-MS, LX, H-HP) screened the literature'), but does not explicitly state the number of reviewers who performed data extraction.
While the text states reviewers worked independently for screening, it does not explicitly report whether multiple data collectors worked independently for data extraction.
The text describes conflict resolution for screening ('Conflicts were resolved by other independent reviewers'), but does not describe processes for resolving disagreements during data extraction.
There is no mention of processes used to obtain or confirm data from study investigators.
While Google Translate is mentioned for translation, there is no description of automation tools used specifically for data extraction (e.g., extraction software, training, validation).

elements.quote: ...if the included article was neither in English nor in Chinese and did not provide an English abstract or full text, we used an online translator (Google Translate) for translation.
elements.reason: The text explicitly describes the method used to translate articles (Google Translate) for non-English/non-Chinese articles.
There is no specification of software used to extract data from figures.

elements.quote: Therefore, we excluded the above literature with the number of unreported infections and selected one of two literature with the same population for inclusion. ... If the paper did not mention the reinfection variant, we classified the reinfection variants based on the WHO standards according to the study period.
elements.reason: The text describes decision rules for selecting data from duplicate populations and resolving inconsistencies regarding reinfection variants.

elements.quote: The complete information extracted included the first author, study period, country, study population, sample size, study design, reinfected variants, time between two positive tests (days), age, reinfection rate, and the number of reinfections.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists the variables for which data were sought in the 'Selection Criteria And Data Extraction' section.

elements.quote: If the paper did not mention the reinfection variant, we classified the reinfection variants based on the WHO standards according to the study period.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the assumption and procedure used to handle missing information regarding reinfection variants.

elements.quote: Additional file 3: Information extraction form.
elements.reason: The supplementary information section lists an 'Information extraction form' as Additional file 3, which is referenced in the main text regarding data inputs.

elements.quote: We used meta-analysis to evaluate the pooled rate of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection in the included studies... we decided to use the logit transformation
elements.reason: The text specifies the outcome (SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate) and the effect measure used for synthesis (logit transformation of the rate).
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting the effect size (e.g., defining high vs. low reinfection rates) are reported in the provided text.

While the text describes converting the rate to a logit transformation, it does not explicitly describe the method used to re-express the synthesized logit results back to the original rate scale for presentation.

elements.quote: However, when the rate is close to 0 or 1, two problems will occur in the meta-regression: the confidence interval may exceed the interval of 0-1, and the variance is squeezed towards 0. Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution... we decided to use the logit transformation
elements.reason: The choice of the logit transformation is justified by the statistical issues that arise when rates are close to 0 or 1 (confidence interval exceeding 0-1, variance issues).

elements.quote: If the paper did not mention the reinfection variant, we classified the reinfection variants based on the WHO standards according to the study period.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the process for deciding eligibility for the variant synthesis (classification of missing data), but does not explicitly describe the eligibility processes for other syntheses (e.g., age, country) in terms of data availability or exclusion criteria specific to those syntheses.

elements.quote: Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution. Four transformations were taken: log transformation, logit transformation, arcsine transformation, and double arcsine transformation. Through the hypothesis test after the transformation, we decided to use the logit transformation
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes the data conversion methods used to prepare data for synthesis, detailing the specific transformations applied to reinfection rates.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, reinfection variant, country, study population, and study type respectively, and the results were shown in Table 1
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes the use of Table 1 to display subgroup analysis results, detailing the tabular structure and data included.

elements.quote: forest plots for each subgroup analysis were shown in Additional file 6
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the use of forest plots to visually display results for subgroup analyses.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, reinfection variant, country, study population, and study type respectively
elements.reason: The basis for grouping studies within the tables and graphs (subgroups like age, variant, country) is clearly reported.
The manuscript uses standard graphical methods (forest plots, meta-regression plots) for displaying results; there is no evidence of non-standard graphs requiring a specific rationale.

elements.quote: Moreover, we used two methods for sensitivity analysis: the first method involved recalculating the combined values by excluding highly biased papers and comparing the differences in results before and after exclusion; the second method involved sequentially excluding each included paper and analyzing whether there were significant differences in results before and after exclusion.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly details the two methods used for sensitivity analysis in the Methods section.
The manuscript describes the sensitivity analyses performed but does not explicitly state whether they were pre-specified or not.

elements.quote: Citations and characteristics for all included studies and all data inputs were shown in Additional file 3.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states that citations for all included studies are provided in Additional file 3.

elements.quote: Citations and characteristics for all included studies and all data inputs were shown in Additional file 3.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states that characteristics for all included studies are provided in Additional file 3.

elements.quote: The study design included cohort study, case-control study, and descriptive study
elements.reason: The study is a systematic review of observational studies, not an intervention review, so intervention details are not required.

elements.quote: For the cohort study, there were 2 studies on the risk of high bias. For casecontrol studies, there was no literature with a high risk of bias. For cross-sectional studies, there were 2 studies on the risk of high bias.
elements.reason: The text summarizes the number of high-risk studies by study design but does not present domain-level and overall risk-of-bias judgements for every included study in tables or figures within the provided evidence.

elements.quote: When the star rating in NOS was less than 3, or the number of 'yes' in JBI was less than 5 [23], we categorized the paper as 'high risk of bias'.
elements.reason: The text describes the criteria used to categorize risk of bias but does not present specific justifications for the risk-of-bias judgement for each included study.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, reinfection variant, country, study population, and study type respectively, and the results were shown in Table 1, and forest plots for each subgroup analysis were shown in Additional file 6.
elements.reason: The text describes subgroup analyses and results but does not display outcome-specific risk-of-bias judgements alongside study results in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: There were 46 cohort studies, 6 case-control studies, and 3 cross-sectional studies. For the cohort study, there were 2 studies on the risk of high bias. For casecontrol studies, there was no literature with a high risk of bias. For cross-sectional studies, there were 2 studies on the risk of high bias.
elements.reason: The text summarizes characteristics (study design) and risk of bias for the main synthesis (55 studies), but does not provide similar summaries for the specific subgroup syntheses mentioned (e.g., by variant, country), thus only partially meeting the 'each synthesis' requirement.

elements.quote: Finally, there were 55 studies included.
elements.reason: The text explicitly states the number of included studies and refers to Additional file 3 for citations and characteristics, thereby identifying the contributing studies.

elements.quote: Through meta-analysis, a total of 14,681,235 subjects were included in the 55 studies, with a total of 111,846 cases of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. The reported range of reinfection rate was between 0% and 28.4%, and the summarized reinfection rate was approximately 0.94% (95% CI : 0.65 -1.35%).
elements.reason: The main meta-analysis results are reported in the text.

elements.quote: the summarized reinfection rate was approximately 0.94% (95% CI : 0.65 -1.35%).
elements.reason: The summary estimate (0.94%) and its precision (95% CI) are explicitly reported.

elements.quote: The first inflection point was on day 154, with a predicted reinfection rate of 1.06% (95% CI : 0.34- 3.29%).

elements.quote: However, the limitations of this study are as follows: first, we did not include the 'grey literature' , which may lack potential relevant studies that meet the inclusion criteria [35]. In addition, the pattern of publication bias in the field of single-arm study with single-group rate is not clear, and funnel plot analysis may lead to inaccurate conclusions. Second, there is still no clear global definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. In the literature of reinfection searched in this study, most of the diagnostic criteria were at least 90 days between two positive laboratory tests. In order to avoid data heterogeneity in metaanalysis while ensuring data quantity, we used previous literature and previous definitions of reinfection in some countries as the criteria for included literature and data extraction in this study. Although we noted that clinical symptoms and real time-PCR or Rapid Antigen test were also important for the definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection, forming a globally harmonized standard definition was definitely beyond the scope of this study. Besides, due to the lack of specific data in the included literature, subgroup analysis of disease severity and vaccination could not be carried out, so it was impossible to explore all the sources of heterogeneity of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rates. Meanwhile, the sample sizes of the literature included in this study were quite different, which might also be the source of heterogeneity in reinfection rates.
elements.reason: The text explicitly identifies and discusses limitations of the evidence and study, including exclusion of grey literature, lack of clear global definition, lack of specific data for subgroup analysis, and sample size differences.
